rereport.closure_text: Case Closed. Closed date : 2018-06-14 08:49:58.697 Case Resolved Dear Constituent     National Grid is installing a new gas main.      The City encourages this type of capital upgrade work.  It will provide dependable gas service to the residents as well as eliminate future emergency repairs.      The City acknowledges that the construction will cause an inconvenience to the residents.    However in the long run the placement of a new gas main is well worth it.      National Grid has to install the gas main first.  Once the main has been installed  then all service connections can be made.      If the City were to make National Grid pave to grade each day's trench work  it would cause multiple seams along the trench.    More importantly  every service connection needs to be cut into the trench.  If we were to pave the trench every day  this would result in 2 by 2 patches inside the trench area  resulting in a very poor final product.     In order to have the best final paving  the City allows the utility company to leave the trench down low until all service connections are made and then pave the trench all at once  resulting in a smooth  and level final trench repair.     Service laterals are topped within 24 hours of excavation.       What the constituent is observing is the trench left down low in preparation for one continuous final paving operation.    The trench is scheduled to be topped Friday  For any questions or concerns  please contact the number listed below    Sincerely     Mark Cardarelli  Supervisor of Utility Coordination and Compliance  Boston Public Works Department  [removed] Office
